area: UI test and check machinery. Covers scripts/ui-mock.mjs, ui-fit-check.mjs, ui-behaviour-check.mjs, ui-cdp.mjs, ui-shots.mjs, ui-contrast.mjs and test/ui-*.test.mjs, plus the page overlays they police: the lid, the card, the machines menu, the done-tray list and the look menu, in ui/index.html, app.css, app.js, board.js, layout.js, focus.js and card.js.
summary: The UI is checked in two tiers. The first is `npm test` (node:test, no browser): it loads the page's pure modules in Node. test/ui-*.test.mjs passes 72 of 72 today on Node 26.13.1. The second tier is three scripts that drive headless Chrome and are not part of npm test: ui-fit-check (geometry and text fit), ui-behaviour-check (interaction and what the page sends) and ui-shots (the PNGs in docs/screens). ui-contrast runs both as a script and inside npm test. All three Chrome scripts point the real page at scripts/ui-mock.mjs, an in-process stand-in for the engine's HTTP API. It serves ui/ and src/shared/ with the real CSP, answers /api from named scenarios, and has /ctl/* control routes (scenario, push, mode, state, log, clear, drop). A scenario is one branch of scenario(name, now). The branch builds compact agent specs, view() expands each into a full AgentView, and world() wraps them into the exact snapshot object the page receives; that object is sent verbatim on /api/state and as the SSE snapshot. view() copies fields one by one: unknown spec fields are dropped, and workspace and sessionId are always null. The exported SCENARIOS list is also imported by test/ui-layout.test.mjs, so every new scenario is laid out at 8 window sizes × 2 detail levels inside npm test, and swept by the fit check at 8 sizes × 2 details × 3 looks. Mock routes are hand-written regexes. Anything unmatched returns 404, and both Chrome checks count a 404 as a failure. Only POSTs are written to the request log the behaviour check asserts on. ui-cdp.mjs is a ~70-line DevTools driver. It spawns process.env.CHROME_BIN, falling back to /Applications/Google Chrome.app, with --headless=new and a temporary profile, then reads DevToolsActivePort. This Mac has no Chrome or other Chromium browser. Running the fit check here crashed at once with an unhandled 'spawn … ENOENT' error and left a wb-ui-* temp profile behind, so neither Chrome check has a verified baseline on this machine. The fit check injects one CHECK function. It fails on: off-screen text or controls; text outside a box it sits in; overlapping text within one layer; clipped text; overlapping board boxes; an overlay (#card, #pop, #trayList, #look) off-screen or over the core or the top band; JetBrains Mono not loading; and any page exception, console error or failed load other than a 401. The exemptions are narrow: .sr text, the one element carrying [data-scroll] (clamped vertically only) and the element carrying [data-clip-ok]. A new overlay is registered by hand in three selector lists inside CHECK, plus a VIEWS entry and an if/else branch that opens it. Unknown view names silently do nothing. ui-behaviour-check drives the page two ways: with in-page element.click(), and with real CDP mouse and keyboard input. It asserts on the mock's POST log (path and body) for each contract rule: answers carry the ids they were drawn for, the click guard after a swap, holding, focus, retryable failures, confirm cards answered by id and withdrawn, and Continue/Forget for earlier agents. The existing overlays all keep off the core and the top band. The card is role=tooltip with pointer-events:none and is placed by layout.js placeCard. The machines menu, done-tray list and look menu are .pop role=dialog elements positioned in app.js. Changed files show only as a list (focus.js filesList: at most 6 paths with +/− counts) behind a quiet "What changed?" link. That link exists only in "more" detail and only while the lid's fit level is below 5 (fs.extras). No fit view or behaviour check clicks it, so it is unverified in a browser (read from code, not run). No diff text exists anywhere in the page. Room is tight: the lid's page is 256–332 px wide and at most 264–322 px tall, side room beside the core is 288 px at 960×900 and 424 px at 1280×680, and there is only about 90 px above or below the core at 1280×680. Both big-button slots are already used on done_*, checks_failed and earlier agents, and several checks pin those pairs.

keyFacts.fact: Chrome location: `export const CHROME = process.env.CHROME_BIN || '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'`. ui-fit-check, ui-behaviour-check and ui-shots all start Chrome through launch() in this file. CHROME_BIN is the only override.

launch({width,height,dpr}) spawns Chrome with '--headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --user-data-dir=<mkdtemp wb-ui-*> --window-size=W,H --force-device-scale-factor=dpr --remote-debugging-port=0 --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check about:blank'. It polls <profile>/DevToolsActivePort 150 times at 100 ms (15 s), opens the page target's webSocketDebuggerUrl with Node's global WebSocket, and enables Page, Runtime and Log. It uses a temp profile, which Chrome requires for remote debugging.

No 'error' listener is attached to the spawned process. Observed here: with no Chrome binary, Node throws an unhandled 'spawn /Applications/Google Chrome.app/... ENOENT', so the friendly 'Chrome did not start (set CHROME_BIN?)' message at line 18 is never reached. The wb-ui-* temp profile is leaked; close() at line 57 is what normally removes it.

This Mac: /Applications holds only Developer.app, Safari, Slack, Utilities and Visual Studio Code. There is no Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave, CHROME_BIN is unset, and there are no puppeteer or playwright browser caches.
accept-real.mjs has its own copy of the Chrome constant (same CHROME_BIN env) and calls Chrome with --screenshot and --virtual-time-budget, only when a screenshots folder is passed.

Driver API returned by launch(): send, ev(expr) (Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise and returnByValue; throws on exceptionDetails), goto(url, ms) (navigate, then a fixed sleep), mouse(x, y, click) (CDP mouseMoved, plus press and release), key(k, {phase: 'down'|'up'|'both', shift}), type(text), shot(file, clip), size(w, h, scale), beforeLoad(source), on(listener), close(). errorsOf(b, skipRegex) collects exceptions, console.error calls and Log errors.

Mock control API, documented in the header: POST /ctl/scenario {name, push?} (sends a fresh snapshot unless push:false and clears confirms); POST /ctl/push {event, data}; POST /ctl/mode {answer: 'ok'|'refuse'|'500'|'drop', auth: 'ok'|'bad', holdMs, down, steps}, merged with Object.assign and never reset; GET /ctl/state; GET /ctl/log; POST /ctl/clear; POST /ctl/drop. startMock({port, host, quiet}) resolves to {port, setScenario(n), close()}. Run standalone with `node scripts/ui-mock.mjs [port]`; any key except 'bad' works.
The request log holds every POST to /api/*, recorded before the token check as {at, method, path, body}. GET requests are never logged.

Mock API routes: GET /api/state, GET /api/stream (retry 1000, then the snapshot, optionally held for holdMs), POST /api/agents/:id/(answer|say|stop), POST /api/confirm/:id, POST /api/command, POST /api/machines/:id/awake. Anything else returns 404 {error:'Not found.'}, which both Chrome checks count as a failure (a Log 'status of 404' error).
mode.answer 'drop' (socket destroyed) and '500' apply to every non-stream /api route. 'refuse' is implemented only inside the agents branch (200 {ok:false, reply:'I could not reach <name>.'}).

In the agents route, a verb that is not answer or say falls through to stop (line 359). The regex only allows answer|say|stop, so widening it without adding a branch would turn the new verb into a stop.

Confirm dispatch: /api/confirm/:id handles c.forget; any other confirm with go:true runs started(c), which is a launch. The typed path in /api/command (yes|ok|do it|go ahead|sure, or no|cancel|never mind|stop) ignores the confirm's kind, so typing 'yes' to a Forget card starts an agent in the mock, and 'no' replies 'OK, I won't start it.'

Forget is the template for a button-initiated confirm. POST /api/command whose text starts with 'forget' and whose focusId names an earlier agent creates confirm {id: 'c'+hex, sentence: 'Forget <name>?', detail: 'It will not show here again. Its folder and branch stay on this computer.'}. go:true deletes the agent and sends a fresh snapshot after 60 ms.

Scenario mechanics: names live in the SCENARIOS array (20 names), and each has a branch in scenario(name, now) that pushes compact specs into raw and returns world(raw, now). An unknown name silently falls through to world([]), the empty 'zero' world.

Spec fields view() understands: id, parentId, rootId, name, task, harness, helperType, model, machineId, state, now, thinking, ageMin, sinceMin, endedMin, turns, toolCalls|calls, toolKinds, recent [[sentence, ok]], spark, helpers, usage|cost, budgetUsd, plan, files, checks, rules, ask (its ageMin becomes createdAt), approvals, says, error, earlier, canContinue, continueReason. sessionId and workspace are hard-coded null, and any other field is dropped.

world() uses DEMO_MACHINES if any agent is off 'laptop', else [LAPTOP]. It always returns mode 'demo', repo null and all harnesses true. Only 'live' overrides these: mode 'live', repo {name, root, head:'abc1234', branch:'main', dirty:3}, one laptop machine. 'live' has no finished agent. The real engine snapshot has no repo.root and adds harnessInfo.

The mock hard-codes state lists in five places: ended states that get an endedAt (72), active states for helper counts (77), states not counted on a machine (251), finished states that accept 'Looks good' (340), and states for 'what needs me' (401). New states such as landed or discarded must be added to each.

Agents that already carry files lists (candidates for a diff): demo 228202 Invoice export (done_checked, 5 files including migrations/0042_invoice_lookup_index.sql, one rule broken); demo 2f4ffc Help pages (done_claimed, 3 files, codex); alldone r0–r3 (2 files each); setaside X (checks_failed); background g3 (a question, with files). The earlier* entries have no files.
npm test coupling: test/ui-layout.test.mjs imports scenario and SCENARIOS from the mock and asserts that boardProblems(G) is empty for every scenario × 8 windows × calm and more.

Fit-check CLI: --size, --scenario, --theme, --detail and --view take comma lists; --quick uses the green look only; --verbose. Without --scenario every scenario runs. Views run when --view is given, or when no --scenario is given. So '--view X' alone also sweeps every scenario; use '--scenario none --view X' to run one view.

Fit-check sweep: SIZES 960x900, 1024x700, 1280x680, 1440x789, 1512x862, 1728x1000, 1920x970, 2560x1300. Each scenario loads /?t=k&still=1 once; then, for each size × detail × look, it sets the look through the #brand menu, waits for animations to settle and runs CHECK. That is 48 checks per scenario.

'boxy' ancestors: '[data-box], button, .chip, .part, .hl, .mach, .page, .pop, #card, .exact code, .to, kbd, label, .readall'. Every text rectangle must lie inside every such ancestor, within 0.75 px horizontally and 1.25 px vertically.
Layers for the text-on-text rule: `p.closest('#card, #pop, #trayList, #look')?.id || 'board'`. Text in the same layer may not overlap (more than 1 px × 1.5 px); different layers may.

The [data-scroll] exemption is vertical only. Rectangles wholly above or below the scroll box are skipped, partly visible ones are clamped top and bottom, and left and right are never clamped. The clipped-text rule exempts only the element carrying data-scroll or data-clip-ok, not its descendants. The off-screen rule for controls ignores scroll clipping.

Overlay rule: each visible #card, #pop, #trayList or #look fails if it is off-screen, if it 'covers the core' (the core is the #board .pkg rectangle, else #core), or if it covers any visible top-band element (#brand, #mode, #repo, #conn, #spend).
In the fit check, exceptions, console.error calls and Log errors other than 'status of 401' all count as failures of the check in progress.

Fit-check views: card-root, card-helper, card-pinned, machines, menu, tray, earlier, exact, reply, notice, confirm, stale, no-key, connecting, reconnecting, motion, swap. Each runs per size × detail with a rotating look. load(sc, q) resets mode {answer, auth, holdMs, down} but not steps, then sets the scenario, the size, goes to /?t=k&still=1<q> (1300 ms), sets the look and settles. The if/else chain has no else branch.

The 'earlier' view is the template for a lid feature with a confirm card: it loads &focus=e-old0, e-old2 and e-old4, &pin=e-old0, and the earlier-many tray list, then clicks [data-act="forget"] and requires the h1 to match /^Forget /.

Behaviour-check harness: ctl() (log and state are GETs); check(name, ok, detail) prints PASS or FAIL; run(name, fn) filters by --only (substrings split on |) and turns a throw into a FAIL. errorsOf skips /status of 401|status of 500|ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE|favicon|ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED|api\/stream/. A fake SpeechRecognition is injected with beforeLoad. The script exits 1 on any FAIL.

open(scenario, {still, theme, detail, mode}): archives and clears the log; resets mode {answer, auth, holdMs, down, steps, ...mode}; sets the scenario with push:false; sets localStorage wb-theme, wb-detail and wb-answered=1; removes sessionStorage wb-later and wb-reviewed; then loads /?t=k[&still=1] and waits 1600 ms. It takes no query parameter, so there is no &focus= or &pin=.

Ways the behaviour check acts on the page: click(sel) and clickIn(sel) call element.click() inside the page, which respects disabled buttons and the click guard. realClick and realClickIn send a CDP mouse press at the element's centre, and the pointer stays there, so the core is held. tabTo(pred) presses Tab until the predicate holds. lidNow() reads 'count / h1 [+also]', and focusNow() names the focused element. askOf(id, who, cmd) builds a permission ask.

Assertions read the mock log, e.g. `p[0].path === '/api/agents/A/answer' && p[0].body.askId === 'pa'`. Forget: `body.text === 'forget it' && body.focusId === 'e-old0'`. Confirm cards: `/api/confirm/` with go true or false. At the end every distinct request shape is printed, with agent, confirm and machine ids replaced by :id.

The earlier-agent block is the closest template for land and discard. It opens the tray, picks a row, checks the lid's words and buttons (fix, forget), then Forget → the question → Cancel, Forget → Do it (the agent leaves state and tray), and Continue posts /say and the agent gets a lane.

Lid click handler: a GUARDED act is ignored until armedUntil. The handler then reads S.agents.get(data-agent), and a missing agent, a data-ask that differs from the agent's current ask, or a data-state that differs from its current state each produce changed() ('That changed. Have another look.'). busy() disables the button and hands its focus to the h1, retry() re-enables it and gives the focus back, and moved() lets the hold go.
GUARDED acts: answer, looksgood, fix, stop, reviewed, later, confirm, reply, parent, pick, forget. The toggles exact, changed, all and readall only flip open[k] and re-render.

Overlay plumbing: escape() closes, in order, look → pop → trayList → voice → reply → input → pin → confirm, else focuses the h1. A document click closes pop, trayList or look when it lands outside them, and unpins the card unless it lands inside #parts, #card, #core, .pop, .mach, #tray or #brand. renderNow() re-renders an open pop or tray list. A resize closes pop and tray.

Placement. The card (placeCard): never within 12 px of the core, never above board.y + topBand − 4, inside the board's 10 px margin; showCard retries narrower widths, then forces it beside the core. #pop: above its connector section, moved beside the core if it would overlap it. #trayList: above the tray, max-height up to the top band, narrowed to the room left of the core (if at least 200 px). #look: under the brand.

#card has role=tooltip, pointer-events:none and z-index 20, so it cannot hold buttons or a scrollable diff. .pop overlays (#pop, #trayList, #look) have role=dialog and z-index 30, and #pop is 300 px wide.

Room, computed from layout.js. The lid's page is 256 px wide (S sizes), 292 (M) and 332 (L). Its maximum height is 296 px at 960×900 and 1024×700, 264 at 1280×680, 304 at 1440×789 and 322 at L sizes. Side room beside the core is 288 px at 960×900, 320 at 1024×700, 424 at 1280×680, 504 at 1440×789, and 510 to 1034 px at L sizes. At 1280×680 the core spans y 160 to 496, leaving about 90 px above and below it.

"What changed?" today: a quiet link, only in 'more' detail and only while fit < 5. It toggles open.changed and shows filesList: up to 6 '<path> +a −d' items, '(hidden by a .gitignore it changed)' for ignored files, and 'and N more'. No diff content exists in the page.

Confirm card: count line 'You said' (also when a button started it, as with Forget), the sentence as h1 (long ones get 'Read all of it'), the detail as the meta line, and the buttons 'Do it' (primary, data-go=1) and 'Cancel' (data-go=0), both bound by data-confirm. The labels are fixed.

Two-button pairs now in use: done_* → Looks good (looksgood) and Ask for a change (reply); checks_failed → Ask it to fix that (fix) and Look later; earlier → Continue (fix) and Forget; failed and stopped → Try again or Continue, and Dismiss.

Checks that pin today's buttons: ui-focus 'every button is bound to what it was drawn for' (skips next, exact, changed, readall and unpick; its fixture has no files); ui-history Continue and Forget; the behaviour check's 'Looks good' checks and the earlier-agent block.

UI unit-test pattern: node:test with assert/strict. A module that imports /shared/ is loaded through module.registerHooks, which maps /shared/ to src/shared/, with a { skip } fallback on older Node. A buttons(html) regex helper collects the data-* attributes of [data-act] buttons.
Debug switches are exactly {static, still, pin, focus} and count only with t=. ui-address.test pins that key set, and that app.js reads its address only through debugSwitches(location.search).

Contrast check: PAIRS is a list of [fg, bg, what, min] custom-property names. palettes() reads only the first block of ':root, :root[data-theme="green"]', ':root[data-theme="black-gold"]' and ':root[data-theme="ivory"]' (app.css lines 10, 43, 76). Values must be plain hex; var() references are followed up to 5 deep. test/ui-contrast.test.mjs enforces it in npm test.

ui-shots: SHOTS entries are [{name, scenario, query?, theme?, detail?, type?}]. Shots are taken at 1440×900, scale 2, and written to docs/screens/<name>.png (tracked files) unless a folder argument is given. A shot cannot click anything; type submits a typed command.
visibleControls() turns C0 control characters and DEL into visible symbols. It does not cover bidi overrides (U+202A–202E, U+2066–2069) or zero-width characters.

AgentView.workspace is the worktree path as a string, with no branch or base. files is { changed, adds, dels, list: [{ path, adds, dels, binary?, large?, untracked?, ignored? }] }. S.meta keeps only mode, repo, harnesses, defaultBudgetUsd and spendTodayUsd from the snapshot.

api.js call() sends JSON with X-Workbench-Token, also on GETs. A 401 marks the key stale. Any other non-2xx status throws a RequestError in plain words. A 200 {ok:false, reply} is thrown with refused=true, and the page shows the reply and keeps the item.

Baseline: `node --test test/ui-*.test.mjs` gives 72 of 72 passing on Node 26.13.1. The Chrome checks have never run on this machine. The CLOUD_PROGRESS counts (for example 1824 fit checks) predate the history views, and git status is clean.

extensionPoints.capability: A scenario whose agents have reviewable work (live mode)
extensionPoints.how:
1. Add names such as 'review' and 'review-long' to SCENARIOS.
2. Add a branch before the 'zero' fall-through, modelled on 'live'. Push laptop-only specs: a done_checked agent with a small diff; a done_claimed agent with a big one; a checks_failed one; a working agent with files; one with files {changed:0}; an earlier agent with files, plus one with canContinue:false.
3. End the branch with `const st = world(raw, now); st.mode = 'live'; st.repo = { name, head: 'abc1234', branch: 'main', dirty: 0 }; st.machines = [{ ...LAPTOP, agents: n, note: `${n} agents` }]; return st;`.
4. Keep diff bodies in a module-level DIFFS map keyed by agent id. Never put them in the spec: view() drops unknown fields, and the snapshot is sent verbatim on every connect.
5. Any new AgentView field (branch, a changes id, a landed or discarded flag) must be added explicitly to view(), mirroring newAgentView in src/shared/events.mjs.
6. If new states are added, update the hard-coded lists at lines 72, 77, 251, 340 and 401.
7. Expect the new scenario to run in npm test (ui-layout boardProblems) and in the fit sweep automatically. Check the spelling, because an unknown name silently gives an empty board.

extensionPoints.capability: Serve an agent's diff from the mock
extensionPoints.how:
1. Add a separate regex before the 404, for example /^\/api\/agents\/([^/]+)\/changes$/ for GET. Do not widen the (answer|say|stop) regex: an unmatched verb there falls through to stop.
2. Return the shape the engine will return: per file, path, status (added, changed, deleted or renamed), adds and dels, binary, large, untracked and ignored flags, and the hunks or text with a truncated flag. Include the id of the state the diff was computed for (branch head or tree hash) so the page can bind to it.
3. Push this GET into `posted` (or a second list), so the behaviour check can assert which agent's diff was fetched; today GETs are invisible.
4. Handle mode.answer === 'refuse' explicitly with 200 {ok:false, reply}. '500' and 'drop' already apply.
5. Give 'review-long' a stress diff: 40 or more files, a 400-character unbroken line, CRLF line endings, tabs, '\ No newline at end of file', binary, large, renamed, deleted and ignored files, a very long path, C0 control characters, U+202E and zero-width characters in both content and paths.

extensionPoints.capability: Land (merge) and discard flows in the mock, with outcomes
extensionPoints.how:
1. Store a kind on each confirm: {id, sentence, detail, kind: 'land'|'discard'|'forget'|'start', agentId, changesId}.
2. Dispatch on kind in both /api/confirm/:id (line 376 today runs started(c) for anything that is not a forget) and the typed yes/no path at lines 380-381.
3. If the design uses /api/command plus a confirm, as Forget does, add command regexes for the new words; otherwise the mock replies 'I did not catch that.'. If it uses dedicated routes (POST /api/agents/:id/land or discard), add a new regex for them.
4. Add a mode.land knob: 'ok' | 'dirty' (uncommitted edits in the person's checkout) | 'moved' (their branch moved on) | 'conflict' | 'changed' (the agent's work changed since it was shown) | 'gone' (folder or branch missing). Each refusal is 200 {ok:false, reply:'<plain sentence>'}, never a 4xx, because a 404, 409 or 500 shows up as a console error that fails both checks.
5. On success, update the agent and send('agents', [a]) after about 60 ms. If the agent leaves the page, send('snapshot', state) instead, as forget does. Optionally send('notice', {text}).
6. Document the new routes and mode keys in the header comment (lines 9-15).

extensionPoints.capability: Reset the new mock knobs between checks
extensionPoints.how: Add every new mode key, with its default, to the ctl('mode', …) call in open() and to fit-check load(); load() does not reset steps today. /ctl/scenario never resets mode, so a missing key carries its last value into every later check. If the page stores review state in storage, add that key to open()'s storage reset as well.

extensionPoints.capability: Register a review/diff overlay in the fit check
extensionPoints.how:
1. Give the overlay an id (for example #review), class 'pop' and a data-box attribute. boxy (line 47) then covers it through .pop and [data-box].
2. Add '#review' to the layer selector at line 65; without it, its text is judged against the board's text and fails 'text on text'.
3. Add '#review' to the overlay loop at line 132; without it, nobody checks that it stays on-screen and off the core and the top band.
4. Put the diff in exactly one element carrying data-scroll, and make its lines wrap (white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere, as #core .exact code.all does at app.css:287-290). The scroll clamp is vertical only, so a horizontally scrolling line fails 'text outside its box' and 'off-screen text'.
5. Keep buttons outside the scroll box, because the off-screen rule for controls ignores scrolling. Alternatively, extend that rule to skip elements clipped by a [data-scroll] ancestor.
6. If the contract is changed so the review may cover the core, add an explicit exception at line 136 and update the 'Checks' paragraph of ARCHITECTURE.md.
7. Add 'review' (and 'land') to VIEWS, with a branch modelled on 'earlier' (lines 231-246): load('review', '&focus=<id>'); clickIn [data-act="changes"]; sleep 900 ms; settle; fail if the overlay is hidden; check.
8. In that branch, also: scroll the box to the bottom and check; open the stress diff and check; click land and discard and check each confirm card (h1 regex); for each mode.land refusal, click and check the #said line.
9. Add an else branch that records an 'unknown view' failure.
10. Iterate with `--scenario none --view review`.

extensionPoints.capability: Behaviour checks for review, land and discard
extensionPoints.where: scripts/ui-behaviour-check.mjs: new run() blocks after line 669; helpers at 33-56
extensionPoints.how:
Mirror the earlier-agent block. open() takes no query, so focus an agent with realClick('.chip[data-id=…]') or a tray row. Then assert from posts() and the GET log:
1. Opening the review fetches that agent's diff and posts nothing.
2. Land and discard ask first: the h1 shows the engine's sentence, Cancel posts /api/confirm/<id> {go:false}, and Do it posts {go:true}.
3. The land request names data-agent and the changes id it was drawn for. A push('agents', [{...a, files: {...}, changesId: 'new'}]) between drawing and clicking gives no POST and 'That changed. Have another look.' (or the engine's refusal).
4. A click right after the core swaps to a land card is ignored (pattern at lines 70-88).
5. Every refusal (each mode.land value, and answer refuse, 500 and drop) keeps the item and re-enables its button, and #said holds plain words: no token or fetch, and no rebase, HEAD or stash (pattern at lines 288-299).
6. Esc closes the overlay and returns focus to its opener (pattern at lines 242-271).
7. Typing 'yes' with the land card on screen posts /api/command with confirmId and does not land anything else (pattern at lines 341-373).
8. Nothing animates at rest with the overlay open (lines 425-430).
9. Discard and land are not offered while the agent is working.
Keep deliberate refusals at status 200, or add their status to the errorsOf skip regex at line 22.

extensionPoints.capability: New lid buttons or links (review, land, discard)
extensionPoints.where: ui/focus.js:152-256 (the lidView cases), ui/app.js:423 (GUARDED), :447-536 (the handler); test/ui-focus.test.mjs:28-52
extensionPoints.how:
1. Build them with big() or quiet() and data { act, agent, state, plus the binding id }.
2. Add the acts to GUARDED.
3. In the handler, check data-state and the binding id against S.agents before sending. Use busy() and retry() and call moved(), as forget does.
4. buttonRow() lays out only one or two labels, and every relevant state already uses both big slots. Either put land and discard in the review overlay's own footer, outside its scroll box, or replace a pair. Replacing a pair breaks the pinned checks: ui-history 79-95 and behaviour 107, 119, 539 and 615-669.
5. Add files to the ui-focus fixture so the new buttons render inside 'every button is bound to what it was drawn for'. Do not add the new acts to that test's skip list.

1. Follow #trayList: a hidden div.pop with role=dialog and data-box, opened by a button carrying aria-expanded and aria-controls.
2. Render it with patchChildren. Place it beside the core: never within G.core ±12 px, never above G.board.y + G.P.topBand, and narrowed to sideRoom(G).
3. Re-render it from renderNow() while it is open, and close it on resize.
4. Add it to escape() and to the document click-outside closers. The .pop class already keeps a pinned card.

rulesToHonour: Node 22 or later, ES modules, no third-party packages. The check scripts have no dependencies, and files in src/shared/ import no node: modules.

Tests use node:test and node:assert/strict, live in test/<module>.test.mjs, need no network and never start a real claude or codex. The Chrome checks stay out of npm test, but anything pure (layout, lid markup, contrast, diff shaping) belongs in npm test.

Plain language in everything a person sees: sentences, not identifiers. Errors never say 'token' or 'fetch'. Precedent: 'Its folder and branch stay on this computer.' Avoid raw git jargon (HEAD, rebase, stash, merge conflict) in sentences.
The lid shows one thing at a time, with at most two big answer buttons laid out by buttonRow(). A label never wraps to squeeze a row, and Allow and Deny carry equal weight.

Binding: every button carries the ids it was drawn for (data-agent, data-ask, data-confirm), never what the centre holds at click time. Requests without an ask id (say, stop, and so land and discard) go only for the data-agent shown, and only while it is still in data-state; otherwise the page says 'That changed. Have another look.' and redraws. A land should also bind to the exact changes the person reviewed.

Clicks are ignored during a swap and for about 760 ms after it (the GUARDED set). Words typed or spoken during a swap are bound to nothing. The person's own moves show at once (moved()), and stream changes are held while the person is in the core.

Anything risky goes through a confirm card, as launches and Forget do. 'Do it' and 'Cancel' post /api/confirm/<id> {go}. A card the page drops (Esc, or picking an agent) is withdrawn with {go:false}. A reply with a new confirm replaces the card; a reply without one drops it without posting.
Refusals are 200 {ok:false, reply}. The page shows the reply, keeps the item, re-enables the button and gives the keyboard focus back.
Focus never lands on an answer when the lid changes and is never dropped. Esc in a list or menu returns focus to its opener, and a row chosen by keyboard takes focus to the lid's sentence.
Overlays never cover the core (keep at least 12 px clear) or the top band (brand, mode, repo, conn, spend), and stay inside the window. The card is never on the core.

Text never leaves its box, nothing is clipped and nothing is off-screen. Long text scrolls only in one marked [data-scroll] box. The contract names only a long command or question there, so a diff box must be added to ARCHITECTURE.md's 'Checks' paragraph.
Contrast: text at 4.5:1 and marks or lit lines at 3:1, in all three looks (green, black-gold, ivory). State never reads by colour alone, and text is at least 10.5 px.

Everything an agent controls is escaped with esc() before it reaches the page. Control characters in commands show as visible symbols, and diffs need the same treatment, extended to bidi and zero-width characters.
No percentage of completion and no estimated finish time.
Debug switches count only with t=, and nothing in the address makes the page send anything. ui-address.test pins the switch keys {static, still, pin, focus}.
Nothing moves at rest, still=1 stops all motion, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured live.
The CSP is default-src 'self' with inline styles only, so no inline script and no external resources.

Where code and ARCHITECTURE.md disagree, fix one of them. The mock mirrors the engine's routes, words and AgentView fields, and its header lists its control routes. Each module's tests are owned with it.
risks: No Chromium browser exists on this Mac, so both Chrome checks crash at launch with an unhandled spawn ENOENT and leak a wb-ui-* temp profile. A first launch of a freshly downloaded app bundle can exceed the 15 s DevToolsActivePort wait (a Gatekeeper scan). A fresh headless profile may also stop on a macOS keychain prompt; --use-mock-keychain is not passed today.

There is no verified browser baseline. The CLOUD_PROGRESS figures predate the history views, so the first implementation step must be a full fit and behaviour run on the current HEAD, to tell existing failures from new ones.

Mock fall-throughs. A typed 'yes' to any confirm, including Forget, starts an agent (ui-mock.mjs:380). A non-forget confirm with go:true runs started() (376). An agents-route verb other than answer or say becomes a stop (359). Land and discard cards would silently 'launch' or 'stop' unless both paths dispatch on kind.
Any route the mock lacks is a 404, which fails both Chrome checks as a console or log error. Refusals must be 200 {ok:false}, or the skip filters must change.
A new /ctl/mode key leaks into every later check unless it is added to open() (behaviour check line 39) and load() (fit check line 199).
Only POSTs are logged, so a GET diff fetch cannot be asserted (which agent, how often) until the mock logs it.

Fit-check blind spots: the [data-scroll] clamp is vertical only, so horizontally scrolling diff lines fail. Buttons inside a scroll box count as off-screen. Only the element carrying data-scroll is exempt from the clip rule. The tray-list pattern scrolls without data-scroll, so do not copy it. An unknown view name or scenario name silently checks nothing.
A forgotten selector registration produces false failures (line 65: 'text on text' against the board) or silently unchecked placement (line 132: the overlay could cover the core unnoticed).

Room is tight: the lid page is 256–332 px wide and at most 9.5em per scroll box, side room is 288 px at 960×900, and there is about 90 px above or below the core at 1280×680. A readable diff fits poorly anywhere that respects 'never on the core'.

The two-button rule clashes with adding Land and Discard to done states. Changing a pair breaks pinned checks: ui-history Continue/Forget, ui-focus binding, and behaviour 'Looks good' and earlier-agent blocks.
'What changed?' is untested in the browser, exists only in 'more' detail, and disappears at fit ≥ 5. If review hangs off it, calm-detail users have no path to the diff.
Trojan Source: visibleControls covers C0 characters and DEL only. Bidi overrides and zero-width characters in an agent's diff or file names would display misleadingly.

Stale binding: a land must name the exact work reviewed. The agent's state can stay done_* while the person's own branch moves, and a follow-up can change files. data-state alone is not enough; a changes id from the diff response or the AgentView is needed.

Diff text must not ride in the AgentView or the snapshot, which is resent on every connect and coalesced over SSE. Large diffs in the DOM also slow the fit check's text-on-text pass, which compares every pair of text rectangles, so cap the lines rendered.
ui-shots writes into the tracked docs/screens/ folder by default.

Mock drift from the engine: the engine snapshot has no repo.root and adds harnessInfo; workspace is always null in the mock; refusal words are copied by hand. New engine routes and words must be mirrored, or the checks test a fiction.
The checks rely on fixed sleeps (700–1600 ms) and include a 21.5 s hold test, so a slower first run on a new Chrome may flake.
openQuestions: Where does the diff live? Options: a [data-scroll] box inside the lid (256–332 px wide); a new .pop overlay beside the core (288–1034 px wide, height between the top and bottom bands); or a review mode allowed to cover the board or core, which needs a contract change and a fit-check exception at line 136.

Where do Land and Discard sit? Options: replacing a done-state button pair, the overlay's own footer, or only through confirm cards. Is a 'You said' count line acceptable on a button-initiated confirm, or should confirm cards carry their own labels, which would need new fields in lidView and the mock?

Are land and discard requests /api/command words plus a confirm (the Forget pattern), or dedicated routes (/api/agents/:id/land, /discard) plus a confirm? The mock and the behaviour check mirror whichever is chosen.
Which id binds a land to what was reviewed: the agent branch's head, a hash of the diff, the person's branch head, or several? Is it carried in the AgentView or only in the diff response?

Do land and discard exist in demo mode? Simulated agents have files but no git. If yes, the demo scenarios need diffs too; if not, the buttons must depend on snapshot mode or a per-agent flag the mock must set.

What does an agent become after land or discard: new states (states.mjs, LOOK marks, contrast pairs, the mock's five state lists), a flag on a done agent, or removal through a fresh snapshot as with Forget?
Can earlier (history) agents be reviewed, landed or discarded? They have folders and branches, but the mock's earlier entries carry no files.
Does a debug switch that opens the review (and triggers a read-only GET) violate 'nothing in the address makes the page send anything'? Prefer clicking in the checks.

Which browser binary will be used on this Mac, and where? The exact Chrome for Testing mac-arm64 executable path inside its .app bundle must be confirmed on disk before writing it into docs or scripts. chrome-headless-shell is untested with --headless=new.
Should the mock log GET requests too, and should the behaviour check's request-shape summary list them?
